answer.rationale: With the contract expiring in 14 days, no auto-renew, and the line already at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer, any switch or dual-sourcing effort this cycle carries unacceptable near-term delivery risk—there isn't time to qualify and ramp an alternate supplier safely. The incumbent has explicitly refused to reopen price this cycle, so negotiate_terms is not currently actionable despite memory_c4's precedent. Renewing the incumbent (verified via memory_c1's archived record for accuracy) preserves continuity and avoids interruption, consistent with c1's stability record and c6's note that longer-term commitments can still capture volume pricing even without a price cut. This does not satisfy finance's 18% cut mandate this cycle, so that gap must be explicitly flagged as unresolved downstream cost/value risk for the next review, where switch_primary_vendor or add_second_source (per c2/c3) can be evaluated with adequate lead time and a capacity buffer in place. Treating this as a full renewal (broad_rollout) rather than a partial test reflects that the whole primary contract is at stake within the 14-day window, not an experimental slice.
